subject: Finova: Decision criteria & next steps (latency, cost, deployment, SLA)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@finova.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Finova: Decision criteria & next steps (latency, cost, deployment, SLA)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we promised to follow up on so we have alignment on next steps and stakeholder responsibilities. I’ve bolded requests where we need inputs from your side.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary use case: live customer chat + personalized recommendations (short responses, ~64–128 tokens typical).
- Key decision criteria called out by your team: latency, unit cost, deployment mode (hosted vs private/VPC), and SLA guarantees (uptime + latency SLOs).

Clarifying questions — please confirm or correct:
1) Latency targets: do you need P95 <= 300ms for 128-token responses, or is P95 <= 500ms acceptable? (we heard both numbers in the meeting) — please confirm the target.
2) Cost target: is there a target cost-per-1k-tokens we should price to for your procurement / TCO exercise? If you don’t have a specific number, is <$2/1k tokens a reasonable internal threshold to evaluate options against?
3) Deployment mode: you mentioned Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, and that the security team may require a VPC/private deployment. Can you confirm if Private deployment (customer VPC / on-prem) is a hard requirement or a preference for later phases?
4) SLA: what uptime and latency SLOs are required by procurement? (e.g., uptime 99.9%, latency targets at P95 / P99)

Stakeholder mapping (please fill in the names/emails for the following so we can route the right artifacts):
- Economic buyer / budget owner: **(who signs the PO / approves spend?)**
- Procurement contact: **(procurement or vendor management contact for contracts / redlines)**
- Security / legal reviewer: **(who will own the security/compliance questionnaire and SOC2 review?)**

What I’ll do from our side:
- Share a short mutual action plan template with proposed milestones (pilot -> pilot eval -> production).
- Share SOC2 + security docs and a short Dedicated/Private deployment pricing stub that maps to the latency/cost targets you confirm.

Requested next steps (action items):
- Alex/Priya: please confirm the answers to the 4 clarifying questions above and share the stakeholder names/emails by EOD Tuesday 11/23 if possible.
- Once I have confirmation, I’ll share a draft mutual action plan and a pricing deck tuned to your targets.

Attachments: Finova_security_questionnaire.pdf (you flagged this on the call — feel free to send the completed copy back and we will route to our security team)

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finova.com>
Date: 2027-11-21T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Finova: Decision criteria & next steps (latency, cost, deployment, SLA)

Marissa — thanks for the summary and for capturing this so clearly. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Latency: Target is P95 <= 300ms for typical chat responses (~128 tokens). We can accept P99 higher, but procurement will ask for a P95 guarantee.
2) Cost: We’re looking for options that show a path to < $1.50 per 1k tokens in production. For the pilot we have more flexibility, but procurement will benchmark against that.
3) Deployment mode: For Phase 1 (pilot) we are open to Redwood hosted, but Phase 2 must be Private (VPC or dedicated) — security has flagged data residency and network controls as blockers for production.
4) SLA: Procurement will expect standard production SLAs — baseline ask is 99.9% uptime and a latency SLO defined at P95 for the 128-token profile. They’ll want remedies for breach (credits).

Stakeholders:
- Economic buyer / budget owner: Rajesh Menon (CTO) — rajesh.menon@finova.com
- Procurement contact: Susan Lee — susan.lee@finova.com
- Security / legal reviewer: Priya Rao — priya.rao@finova.com (I’m copied here)

I’ve attached the current security questionnaire as requested. We’ll fill in any additional fields you send back.

Best,
Alex
Director, Product Engineering | Finova

Marcus / Laura — forwarding Alex’s reply and the filled-in stakeholder mapping. Key asks from Finova: P95 <= 300ms (128 tokens), target cost < $1.50/1k tokens in production, pilot can be hosted but production must be Private/VPC, procurement expects 99.9% uptime + latency SLO with credits.

Actions I need from you:

- Laura: procurement/legal — can you confirm whether the standard Redwood SLA (99.9%) plus credit language is feasible for a production Private deployment? Also note any typical lead times for DPA / SOC2 artifact share.

I’ll coordinate a follow-up call with Rajesh and Susan — would like to get an exec intro on next week if possible. 

Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-21T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Finova: Decision criteria & next steps (latency, cost, deployment, SLA)

Thanks Marissa — I’ll put together the two scenarios. Preliminary notes below so we can align before I build slides: 

- Pilot (hosted): optimized small model variant, autoscaled pool; expected P95 ~ 200–300ms for 128-token responses under expected QPS (we need Alex’s expected concurrency numbers). Cost estimate: pilot-level pricing will be higher per token but manageable for evaluation.
- Prod (Private / Dedicated): with reserved GPUs + KV-prefix caching and quantized model we can show a path to <$1.50/1k tokens at scale. The big lever is utilization and batching — we’ll show sensitivity to QPS and average token length.

Assumptions I’ll use (please confirm):
- Typical payload: 1 request = 128 tokens output average; 20 tokens input average.
- Pilot QPS: 10–25 concurrent requests considered (tunable).
- Prod QPS: assumption TBD — Marissa, can you ask Alex for target concurrent users / peak QPS?

I’ll draft pricing and an SLA note. Laura — can you flag any standard SLA exceptions we should prepare for Private deployments (compliance lead times, support SLAs, etc.)? I’ll target a deck by EOD 11/23.

Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
